data.title: What should be considered when replacing a dispersant in an existing SC formulation?
data.answer:
Replacing a dispersant in a suspension concentrate (SC) formulation requires more than matching its chemical type or dosage. Differences in adsorption behaviour, active ingredient compatibility and interactions with other formulation components can affect particle size stability, viscosity and redispersibility. Comparative evaluation should include dispersion efficiency, rheology, accelerated storage stability and dilution behaviour.

Aidigro offers dispersants for evaluation in different SC formulation systems. Customers can explore the Product Finder or contact our technical team to discuss suitable alternatives.

data.title: Why can an SC formulation develop hard sediment during storage despite showing good initial stability?
data.answer:
Initial physical stability does not necessarily predict long-term storage behaviour. Hard sedimentation may result from particle aggregation, crystal growth or insufficient suspension structure. Temperature fluctuations and interactions between formulation ingredients can further influence sediment formation. Increasing viscosity alone may not resolve the problem.

Evaluation of particle size distribution, rheology, dispersant compatibility and storage behaviour is important in identifying the underlying cause. Our technical team can assist in identifying suitable Aidigro ingredients for evaluation.

data.title: Can two emulsifiers with similar specifications perform differently in the same EC formulation?
data.answer:
Yes. Emulsifiers with similar general specifications may differ in molecular composition, hydrophilic-lipophilic balance and compatibility with the solvent and active ingredient. These differences can influence emulsion formation, droplet size and stability upon dilution.

Comparative testing should consider different water hardness levels, dilution ratios and temperatures. Selection should be based on performance in the intended formulation rather than specifications alone.

Customers can explore available emulsifiers through our Product Finder or contact us for product selection and technical support.

data.title: Does improving wetting performance necessarily compromise microbial viability in biological formulations?
data.answer:
Not necessarily. Wetting performance and microbial compatibility are influenced by surfactant chemistry, concentration, microorganism type and formulation conditions. A surfactant that provides effective wetting may still be compatible with certain biological systems, but this cannot be assumed across different organisms.

Selected Aidigro ingredients have demonstrated wetting improvement while maintaining biological compatibility under evaluated conditions. Both properties should be assessed together when developing biological crop protection formulations.

Contact our technical team for supporting compatibility information on selected Aidigro ingredients.

data.title: Is complete reformulation necessary to improve wetting in an existing biological pesticide?
data.answer:
Not always. Direct addition of a suitable wetting agent may be considered where the existing formulation is physically stable but requires improved wetting performance. However, the added ingredient may influence microbial viability, formulation stability and storage behaviour.

Direct incorporation, reformulation and tank-mix addition are different development approaches, each requiring appropriate evaluation. Aidigro offers selected ingredients for investigating these options.

Contact our technical team to discuss suitable wetting agents and evaluation approaches.

data.title: Why can irrigation water penetrate unevenly into soil even when sufficient water is applied?
data.answer:
Uneven water penetration may result from soil water repellency, differences in soil texture, compaction or preferential water flow. In water-repellent soils, irrigation water may bypass certain areas rather than wetting the soil uniformly.

Soil-wetting agents can improve contact between water and soil surfaces, supporting more uniform wetting and water distribution. SoilHydrate is KLK OLEO's soil-wetting agent range developed for direct field application. Performance depends on soil conditions, application rates and irrigation practices.

Explore our SoilHydrate range for product information, application guidance and supporting field trial results.

data.title: What should be evaluated when qualifying an alternative agrochemical surfactant supplier?
data.answer:
Supplier qualification should consider more than product specifications and pricing. Important factors include batch-to-batch consistency, impurity profiles, formulation performance, regulatory documentation and supply reliability.

Even products with similar specifications may behave differently in a formulation. Comparative laboratory evaluation and appropriate stability testing are recommended before substitution.

KLK OLEO can provide relevant technical information and samples to support qualification of selected Aidigro products. Customers can explore our Product Finder or contact us for further information.

data.title: What information should be provided when requesting an alternative surfactant or formulation recommendation?
data.answer:
Providing the formulation type, active ingredient, existing surfactant system and intended performance requirements helps identify suitable alternatives. Information on current formulation challenges, regulatory restrictions and target market is also useful.

For commercial evaluation, estimated volume and destination country can help clarify supply requirements.
